cells.tense: Care is being given at the pace the growing thing can actually take.
cells.act: surrender the outcome and keep the act
cells.ask: Keep giving the care, and hand the finished shape of it over. Say to yourself, once: what becomes of it from here is not mine to carry.
cells.core:
You give care at the size that lets things grow, and then you stay out of the way. You water, you wait, you don't keep checking whether it worked. That isn't distance — it's the kind of attention a slow thing can use. Where care is the work, the good version looks like this: hands open, growth happening without your hand on it.

If that's where you stand, the next edge is releasing the result. The caring is already yours. The small act is putting the outcome down: keep doing what you do, and stop carrying where it lands. Whatever comes of it comes.

Harder in a week when something is fragile. But the care was not the result. Releasing is what lets it be someone else's growth, not your project.
cells.sheetLine: You give the care and release the result.
cells.place: Where care is the work, and the growth is slow

cells.tense: By the time anything has had a chance to grow, the whole outcome has already been rehearsed and corrected.
cells.act: let the path show itself instead of forcing clarity
cells.ask: Stop deciding the shape of something you're tending. For one stretch, only give what it asks for — corrections can wait.
cells.core:
Care picked up speed. What's growing doesn't get to show its own direction for long before a fix arrives — a correction, a worry, a plan for how it should go. It looks like attention and it isn't: it's your hand on the thing, moving it. Under that much care, growth stops being allowed and starts being managed. When the care is this thick, the thing it's for can't be seen.

So leave a growing thing be, and let a stretch pass without your edit. Not less love — less motion. Let it show what it wants to be before you arrive with the fix. You don't have to like what it does.

One less correction than you want to make. The care stays. The grip goes, and what's growing gets room to answer for itself.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing a growing thing that wanted tending.
cells.place: Where care is the work, and the growth is slow

cells.tense: For a long while now, care has been kept at arm's length and called self-sufficiency.
cells.act: choose the light to steer by and turn toward it
cells.ask: Face something you'd like to grow, just for yourself, and take a step toward it this week — small enough for a flat day.
cells.core:
Here, nothing is being tended, and the empty stretch gets called independence. Care isn't deliberately withheld — it went quiet. What wanted growing was left, and the days don't ask about it, and you don't either. There's a place your attention goes, and this stopped being it some time back.

Growth needs a direction it actually wants, not a bigger push. So turn toward something you'd like to become, yours alone, and face it once this week. Not a plan, not a promise — a step small enough to take when you're flat. The draw toward what you want is still working. It's been pointed away from you. Face it again, and something starts moving that doesn't need pushing.
cells.sheetLine: You keep everything at a distance and call it independence.
cells.place: Where care is the work, and the growth is slow

cells.tense: Care is being given steadily, and you describe it as nothing much.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: Notice a piece of care you carry out of habit rather than want, and quit carrying it — let it wait, or let someone else take it.
cells.core:
People are being cared for by you, and your account of it is that you're just getting on. Part of your days runs on your attention — a person steadied, a situation kept alive — and the part of you that feels it is empty. Nobody chose this at the start. It accumulated, so slowly that no single piece looks like the whole. You're holding it up, and nobody thinks to ask how you are.

So take a piece and put it down. Not a dramatic resignation — a single habit of tending that's no longer yours, left aside. It may be expected of you; it may go unnoticed. Either way you get to see what's underneath, which is usually lighter. What you release makes room. The next question gets to be yours.
cells.sheetLine: You carry care nobody asked you to and call it ordinary.
cells.place: Where care is the work, and the growth is slow

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is the Too Much cell's 'other people have learned to answer before they finish a sentence' — the record gives controlling care, not the other person's adaptation, so I cut it and kept the mechanism to how care is delivered without being asked for. A reader could reasonably say the person has never felt controlling, only tired; the asks survive being wrong anyway because each one can be done alone, with nothing to fix and no one to please. The line that serves me more than them is 'you were doing this before anyone asked,' which sounds like absolution; it is replaced with the plainer claim that the role has no chosen beginning, which is what the record actually supports.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim was that the person keeps distance from what people bring them and from what they want — the record locates a block, not that specific distance, so I cut the diagnosis and kept it to the plain fact that nothing is being tended here. A reader could reasonably say they tend plenty but it never takes; the asks survive being wrong because each is one small move with no outcome promised, doable alone. The line that served me more than them was 'you're just getting on with it' in the Too Much cell, which flattered the person's modesty rather than describing the mechanism; it is now about care arriving before it was asked for. The one-thing and one-week frames are cut back so the acts differ in shape and not all carry a clock.
